prerequisites.reason: Discrete and continuous are the two main kinds of random variable.
A probability distribution describes how a random variable's values vary.
Mass functions belong to discrete random variables.
A mass function is one of the two classes of probability function.
Density functions belong to continuous random variables.
A density function is one of the two classes of probability function.
A discrete CDF accumulates the mass function's probabilities.
A continuous CDF accumulates area under the density.
Other probabilities are built from cumulative ones.
A percentile is the CDF read backwards.
The expected value weights each value by its mass-function probability.
Variance measures spread around the expected value.
Comparing a distribution's mean and variance with a sample's needs both defined.
The binomial is a named discrete distribution with its own mass function.
The probability formula applies only once the conditions hold.
Binomial ranges are found from cumulative binomial probabilities.
A binomial's shape is the pattern of its probabilities.
A binomial's mean np is its expected value.
Sampling without replacement breaks the constant-probability condition.
The Poisson is a named discrete distribution with its own mass function.
Lambda's meaning comes from the Poisson setting.
Approximating a binomial needs the binomial first.
The Poisson's mean equals its variance.
Location and scale act on a density curve.
Comparing location and scale with the mean and standard deviation needs both.
The normal's mean and standard deviation are its location and scale.
Normal probabilities are areas under a density curve.
The standard normal is one member of the normal family.
The standard normal is the normal's standard form.
Normal probabilities are read from the standard normal.
Above and between probabilities come from cumulative ones.
Finding a value from a probability is a percentile question.
The approximation reduces to a normal probability calculation.
The approximation uses the binomial's mean and spread, and its shape decides when it works.
The uniform is a continuous density.
The exponential is the waiting time in a Poisson process.
The exponential is a continuous density.
A shape parameter is the third kind of parameter, beside location and scale.
Other shapes are described against the normal.
A probability plot compares sample and theoretical percentiles.
A normal probability plot checks data against the normal.
Reading departures needs the plot first.
